name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in CI with dry-run mode for a week, then enforce rules. It lets us test the tool’s impact without risking real PRs, proving its value first. The trade-off is slower feedback loops during dry-run, but that’s safer than breaking workflows. After a week, we enforce rules to lock in quality gains.

name: Gauge
text: Dry-run normalizes noise by letting PR-Agent’s edits sit unchecked in PRs, so the "safe" test actually trains the team to ignore its output—until we enforce it and break workflows anyway. Instead, run PR-Agent in CI with a *read-only* mode that logs violations but never edits; after two weeks, if the logs show clear, actionable patterns, we enforce the rules. Settle it by requiring the lead to state the decision and attach the violation log showing at least 3 distinct, fixable issues.
